scope: Manual review of all remaining p1927 interfaces, including both critical-radius members, using frozen source/ambient notes and directly inspected pinned library declarations.

rows.query: Repository-wide Markov reward process, Bellman and LSTD search; inspect measurable kernels, probability normalization and infinite trajectory construction.
rows.result: Homogeneous probability transitions and trajectories have representations, but no dedicated discounted reward-process interface was located.
rows.gap: The discounted reward process still needs its reward functional and a measure-valued interpretation of the source's unspecified real kernel signature.

comparisons.D1: The source writes P:X times X to real on a potentially general state space, without a reference measure for a transition density; Kernel X X instead assigns a measurable measure to each state, with IsMarkovKernel ensuring probability. Preserve that representational gap. Gamma is strictly in (0,1), rewards are known real functions with no [0,1] bound in this definition, and this is policy evaluation with no action space introduced; arbitrary unbounded rewards need convergence/integrability for a discounted value.

rows.query: Search stationary pair sampling and invariant kernels; inspect Invariant, measure composition-product, iIndepFun and IdentDistrib.
rows.result: Invariant probability law and its conditional pair law can be specified, with independent identical repetitions at the pair level.
rows.gap: The iid stationary-pair experiment must still be assembled from a probability invariant measure and its transition kernel.

comparisons.D3: mu compProd P is the law of (X,X') with X~mu and X' conditional on X through P, retaining dependence between the coordinates. Invariance plus probability makes both marginals mu; it does not make them independent, reversible, or imply unique stationary measure. iIndepFun and identical law apply across n pairs, not consecutive pairs from one trajectory; the source expressly excludes that dependent sampling extension.

rows.query: Inspect real geometric-series identity under 0<=gamma<1 and compare the source H=(1-gamma)^-1.
rows.result: The exact reciprocal effective horizon is ordinary real arithmetic, and the inspected theorem identifies it with the discount-weight sum.
rows.gap: The reciprocal definition is directly expressible, and the geometric-series identity gives its interpretation as total discount weight for the stated gamma range.

comparisons.D14: Gamma in (0,1) supplies both hypotheses of tsum_geometric_of_lt_one; its right side is exactly H, so no domain extension, limiting gamma=1 convention, or stochastic model is required for this scalar definition.

rows.query: Search Mercer expansion, compact spectral decomposition and RKHS kernel semantics; inspect scalar specialization of RKHS.kernel and eigenvector predicate.
rows.result: The reproducing kernel and individual eigenpairs can be represented; no Mercer theorem matching the pointwise infinite expansion was located.
rows.gap: The Mercer expansion still requires its measure-dependent eigenfunction system, convergence and topological hypotheses beyond the kernel and eigenvector primitives.

comparisons.D11: The source assumes unspecified conditions for K(x,z)=sum_j mu_j phi_j(x)phi_j(z), with nonnegative eigenvalues and L2(mu)-orthonormal eigenfunctions. HasEigenvector does not supply orthonormality, completeness, sorting or pointwise versions of L2 classes; the operator-valued RKHS.kernel must be specialized to real scalar outputs. Do not insert compactness/full support hypotheses or replace the pointwise series with a finite-dimensional matrix spectrum or merely an L2 expansion.

rows.query: Search uniform eigenfunction bounds and inspect supremum-bound equivalence against the source's pointwise supremum norm.
rows.result: Supremum inequalities can encode the common bound after establishing boundedness/nonemptiness, without assuming continuity or replacing supremum by essential supremum.
rows.gap: The uniform eigenfunction bound still requires specified pointwise eigenfunction representatives and a single bound valid across all indices and states.

comparisons.D13: The norm is sup over every x of |phi_j(x)|, not an L-infinity essential norm; L2(mu) equivalence classes alone cannot supply values on null sets. Preserve one finite kappa for every j>=1; the printed max over infinitely many j does not establish that an index attains it. This extra hypothesis is used for the fast rate and does not follow just from orthonormality or the kernel's diagonal bound.

rows.query: Inspect complete-convex-set projection existence and variational characterization; search projection uniqueness and nonexpansiveness in Projection/Minimal.
rows.result: The Hilbert projection existence theorem applies to a nonempty complete convex subset, and the variational inequality supports uniqueness and nonexpansiveness.
rows.gap: The projection map still needs a nonempty L2-closed class and the selection, uniqueness and nonexpansiveness consequences of the inspected projection theorems.

comparisons.D4: Take F to be real L2(mu), so closedness gives completeness in the L2 metric; require G nonempty, which convexity and closedness alone do not imply. The existence theorem minimizes ||f-g||, equal to the printed ||g-f|| by norm symmetry. It is a general convex-set projection, not necessarily linear or a submodule projection. No RKHS-norm completeness may replace L2 closedness when this definition is later specialized.

rows.query: Search Bellman/projected contraction semantics; inspect complete metric contraction fixed-point existence/uniqueness, projection characterization and stationarity.
rows.result: Banach fixed-point existence and uniqueness are available once the projected Bellman map is a contraction of a nonempty complete space.
rows.gap: The projected Bellman map still needs to be well-defined on L2 and shown contractive using stationarity and the convex projection's nonexpansiveness.

comparisons.D5: T(f)=r+gamma P f requires an L2 reward and a well-defined transition operator on L2 classes; invariance supplies the measure relation used to derive its norm contraction, not a ready Bellman theorem. Combine gamma in (0,1) with a 1-Lipschitz projection, on a nonempty closed class or complete ambient L2. The inspected fixed-point theorem handles the final existence/uniqueness step only after these obligations, and does not identify theta-star with the unprojected true value.

rows.query: Search population kernel LSTD and projected Bellman equation; inspect RKHS reproducing identity, complete-convex projection and contraction fixed-point theorems.
rows.result: Projection, contraction and reproducing-kernel ingredients support the proposed characterization but leave the RKHS-to-L2 embedding assumptions unresolved.
rows.gap: The population kernel LSTD fixed point still requires L2-closedness of the RKHS image and a justified bridge to its covariance-operator equation.

comparisons.D8: Setting G=H in (6) inherits L2 closedness from D4, which is not automatic from completeness in the RKHS norm. The auxiliary (9) is Sigma_cov theta=Sigma_cov r+gamma Sigma_cr theta; footnote 3 assumes r in H or proposes Pi(r), without rewriting the printed definition. Establish the embedding/equivalence before applying Banach; a projected theta-star can differ from true V-star, and the upper estimation bound does not erase approximation error.

rows.query: Inspect joint transition measure and Bochner integral; compare source residual second moment with the centered variance definition.
rows.result: The printed quantity is an integral of the squared residual under the stationary pair law, not automatically the library's centered variance.
rows.gap: The residual second moment still needs its stationary pair law and integrability, with a separate zero-mean proof if it is to be identified with variance.

comparisons.D16: Integrate (theta(X)-r(X)-gamma theta(X'))^2 under mu compProd P. Projection can leave a residual with nonzero mean unless further structure supplies zero mean, so subtracting its mean changes (16). Appropriate L2 membership and stationary marginals give finite second moment; Bochner's nonintegrable-zero fallback is not a noise convention, and the source does not require strictly positive noise in this definition.

rows.query: Inspect RKHS point-evaluation bound and scalar kernel specialization; search uniform diagonal kernel bounds.
rows.result: The reproducing estimate uses the diagonal kernel norm; the common bound b is a separate hypothesis.
rows.gap: The uniform diagonal constraint still needs the scalar-kernel identification and a bound valid at every state.

comparisons.D12: For real scalar positive kernels, identify the operator-valued kernel norm on the diagonal with nonnegative K(x,x), obtaining |f(x)|<=||f||_H sqrt(K(x,x)). Then the source bound yields uniform evaluation control by b; neither boundedness nor a strictly positive b follows just from the RKHS class. Preserve the supremum over all x and do not weaken it to an essential bound under mu.

rows.query: Search projected fixed-point radius and RKHS/uniform norm control; inspect evaluation bound and supremum equivalence.
rows.result: The two norms can be represented, but their simultaneous radius constraint is model-specific.
rows.gap: The radius condition still needs RKHS membership, a pointwise uniform bound and valid division by the kernel bound b.

comparisons.D15: R is any user-specified upper bound on both ||theta-star-r||_H and 2||theta-star||_infinity/b, not a necessarily minimal radius or ||theta-star||_H. The source norm is a pointwise supremum; r membership/projection remains the footnote convention. A zero kernel or b=0 needs an explicit resolution before using the ratio; total real division must not hide that degeneracy.

rows.query: Search critical radius, localized kernel complexity and smallest positive solution; inspect IsLeast and square root domains and compare both source variants.
rows.result: IsLeast expresses positive feasible membership and minimality, but supplies neither convergence of the spectral series nor existence of a least positive feasible radius.
rows.gap: The critical radii still need convergent spectral complexity and nondegenerate parameters that ensure an attained positive least solution, with the two variants' spectra and slopes kept distinct.

comparisons.D17: Use IsLeast of {delta>0: C(delta)<=sqrt(n) R delta/(H(gamma) zeta)}. Mere monotonicity does not prove attainment or a positive least solution; an all-zero spectrum makes every positive delta feasible with no least member. Real tsum of a nonsummable series and sqrt defaults cannot define the intended complexity. zeta>0 is stated, but the fast-rate substitution kappa*sigma can be zero without a supplied limit convention.
comparisons.D22: The lower-bound slope is sqrt(n) barR(1-gamma)/(2 barSigma), corresponding algebraically to the upper form only with the right parameter substitution. Its mu_j are the pre-specified family envelope, not necessarily the actual instance eigenvalues mu_j(P); do not replace the envelope by an instance spectrum in Regime B. Positive barSigma and nondegenerate spectrum/scale are needed for the asserted least positive radius; preserve the factor 2.

rows.query: Search horizon-dependent kernel LSTD parameter regimes; inspect closed interval and real square-root domains against (32a).
rows.result: The explicit scalar inequalities are representable, but no specialized parameter-regime theorem was located.
rows.gap: Regime A still needs its exact spectral and horizon-dependent inequalities with nondegenerate denominator parameters.

comparisons.D26: Require barR >= [1/(6(1-gamma))] max{gamma/sqrt(mu_1),2/b}; the noise constraint applies to barSigma squared in the closed interval [(1+gamma)/(5(1-gamma)),(1+gamma)/(1-gamma)]. Preserve 6,5 and both endpoints. Gamma in (0,1) fixes the horizon denominator, but mu_1=0 and b=0 are not resolved by generic sqrt/division conventions. Do not infer a theorem for every family just from satisfying these scalar bounds.

rows.query: Search horizon-independent LSTD regime and inspect half-open interval and square-root definitions against (32b).
rows.result: The exact scalar domain can be written using a half-open interval and real inequalities; it is separate from the existence of hard MRP families.
rows.gap: Regime B still needs the stated radius and half-open noise constraints with positive spectral and kernel-bound denominators.

comparisons.D27: barR >= max{1/(2 sqrt(mu_1)),2/(gamma b)} and barSigma squared lies in (1/8,1], strictly excluding the lower endpoint. Gamma remains in (0,1), so this differs from Regime A's horizon-growing noise interval. Preserve the source's roles of barR and barSigma despite the reversed pair printed in Theorem 2(b); no zero-eigenvalue or zero-b convention is supplied.

rows.query: Search statistical/effective dimension and largest qualifying spectral index; inspect finite maximum and frozen eigensequence-order notes.
rows.result: A finite maximum can select the largest qualifying index once that set is proved finite and nonempty; it is not automatically a count.
rows.gap: The statistical dimension still needs finiteness and nonemptiness of the qualifying index set without silently imposing eigenvalue ordering.

comparisons.D23: d_n is max{j>=1:mu_j>=delta_n^2}, with equality included, not sum of threshold indicators or trace of a resolvent. Summable nonnegative eigenvalues and positive delta give finitely many qualifying indices, but do not guarantee any qualify. Without a stated decreasing order, their largest index can differ from their number; Finset.max' requires the missing nonemptiness proof instead of assigning zero by default.

rows.query: Search Analysis and Probability for kernel regularity, statistical dimension, critical radius and local complexity; inspect spectral-index and critical-radius primitives for a matching statistical inequality.
rows.result: No declaration in the searched revision packages this sample-dependent regularity condition; generic order and arithmetic do not add a substantive result about it.
rows.no_related_reason: The condition links the paper's own d_n and delta_n to its noise/radius/horizon parameters; searched kernel and spectral infrastructure did not provide a relevant regularity theorem.
rows.gap: The sample-dependent kernel regularity inequality remains a separate hypothesis with its universal-constant scope left as stated by the source.

comparisons.D24: Preserve [2 barSigma/(barR(1-gamma))]^2 d_n >= c n delta_n^2, using the lower-bound critical radius and largest-index statistical dimension. The prose does not fully specify whether one c covers all n and parameter choices; do not silently strengthen or weaken that quantifier or infer the condition from trace class alone. It is required for Theorem 2 by adjacent main-text commentary.

rows.query: Search trace-class kernels and uniformly bounded eigenfunctions; inspect pointwise supremum and RKHS evaluation estimates and compare the two exact constraints in (29a).
rows.result: Uniform bounds have order/evaluation infrastructure, but neither the eigenfunction constant nor the spectral trace bound is automatic from an RKHS.
rows.gap: The lower-family spectral conditions still require the common eigenfunction bound and a genuinely convergent nonnegative eigenvalue sum bounded by b squared over four.

comparisons.D19: Require the actual pointwise eigenfunction bound kappa=2 for every j and sum_j mu_j<=b^2/4, not b^2 or a centered covariance trace. The two explicit constraints are retained together; an ordinary real tsum defaults to zero for nonsummable input and cannot certify trace class. Pointwise versions and convergence must be established, without inventing a maximum-attaining eigenfunction index.

rows.query: Inspect uncentered covariance-operator integral, rank-one orientation, RKHS reproducing identity and conditional pair measure for population LSTD operators.
rows.result: The covariance application matches an uncentered feature second moment; rank-one integration also represents the ordered cross moment.
rows.gap: The population operators still need measurable square-integrable feature maps and the ordered cross-moment construction under the stationary pair law.

comparisons.D7: Phi_X=kerFun H X 1 in the real scalar specialization. rankOne Phi_X Phi_X' maps f to f(X') Phi_X, giving inner(g,Sigma_cr f)=E[g(X)f(X')], not its adjoint. Sigma_cov uses X twice and covarianceOperator_apply matches without centering the feature law. The notation mu times P is conditional compProd, not independent product mu times mu; no reversibility or symmetry of Sigma_cr follows from stationarity.

rows.query: Inspect stationary measures, joint pair law, L2 norm and covariance/eigenpair interfaces against the lower-family measure convention.
rows.result: The library ingredients permit an instance-indexed stationary experiment and covariance operator while keeping the reference measure separate.
rows.gap: The lower-bound instance still needs its chosen stationary measure, sampling law, error norm and spectral data consistently indexed by the transition kernel.

comparisons.D28: Fix the regime's RKHS and reward r in it, then vary P; choose stationary probability mu(P) for sampling, loss and covariance. The bare mu now denotes Lebesgue measure, but the LB norm explicitly means L2(mu(P)), not Lebesgue L2. eLpNorm at 2 can retain infinite error until integrability is established; covariance uses the uncentered feature law and actual eigenpairs mu_j(P),phi_j(P). These differ from the prescribed envelope determining lower delta_n, especially in Regime B, and stationarity alone does not give uniqueness.

rows.query: Search empirical covariance/cross-covariance and LSTD; inspect rank-one application and reproducing identity.
rows.result: Finite averages of the inspected rank-one maps give the empirical operators with the source's feature order.
rows.gap: The empirical operators still need the indexed feature-map sums and exact normalization, with cross-covariance order preserved.

comparisons.D9: Sum over n observed pairs, preserving repeated observations, then multiply by 1/n with n positive. Covariance uses Phi_xi in both slots and maps f to n^-1 sum f(x_i)Phi_xi; cross-covariance uses successor in the second slot and maps f to n^-1 sum f(x_i')Phi_xi. Neither is centered, the denominator is n rather than n-1, and cross-covariance need not be self-adjoint or positive. This construction does not prove existence of the later nonsymmetric empirical fixed point.

rows.query: Inspect RKHS uniform evaluation, pointwise supremum bounds and residual-square integral for lower-family validity constraints.
rows.result: Norm and noise primitives can express the two constraints; their joint validity is an instance-specific assumption.
rows.gap: The family bounds still need RKHS membership, pointwise norm control and the uncentered residual noise with nondegenerate scaling.

comparisons.D20: Require max{||theta-star-r||_H,2||theta-star||_infinity/b}<=barR and sigma(theta-star)<=barSigma. Noise is the square root of D16's uncentered second moment, not a centered standard deviation by definition. The construction assumes r and theta-star belong to H; preserve b's denominator issue and true-value realizability specific to the lower families instead of importing it into the general projected upper target.

rows.query: Search valid MRP family and uniform spectral/noise conditions; inspect underlying norm and moment primitives against the all-members quantifier.
rows.result: The constituent bounds can be expressed with existing norms and moments, but the family predicate is specific to this paper.
rows.gap: Validity still needs a family-wide conjunction of the exact spectral, eigenfunction, radius and residual-noise conditions.

comparisons.D21: For every member require both (29a) and (29b), sharing barR,barSigma and the stated eigenfunction bound kappa=2 and trace bound. This is a definition of valid families; it neither proves such a family exists nor implies a minimax lower bound for every valid family. Maintain instance-dependent stationary measures and distinguish the prescribed spectral envelope in later families from actual instance eigenvalues.

rows.query: Search minimax probability lower bound and iid stationary experiment; inspect finite product law, probability evaluation and infimum/supremum inequalities.
rows.result: The experiment law and bounded probability extrema are available ingredients; no matching kernel-LSTD minimax lower-bound theorem was located.
rows.gap: The minimax tail-risk statement still needs a measurable data-to-function estimator class and a hard-family argument under each instance's stationary-pair experiment.

comparisons.D25: Form the n-fold product of each instance's mu(P) compProd P law, evaluate the event squared L2(mu(P)) error >= c1 barR^2 delta_n^2, then take supremum over the family and infimum over all measurable estimators into real-valued functions, not only H-valued or LSTD estimators. Event measurability and admissible nonempty domains are obligations; probability bounds give bounded extrema once set up, with universal c1,c2 retained. Delta_n is family-prescribed, and Theorem 2 asserts existence of hard families rather than hardness of every valid family.
